findings: All tested corrections improve national FMAM rainfall-amount CRPSS over raw ECMWF in 1993–2016 (raw -0.585; corrected -0.059 to -0.005). Performance varies for monthly tercile probabilities: 0 method–month combinations score below the raw model on RPSS.

Accounting for the whole search. With Holm adjustment across all 60 method–target comparisons, the amount (CRPS) screening passes are none, and the tercile (RPS) passes are Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Feb, Mar), Power Transformation (Feb, Mar) and Empirical Quantile Mapping (Feb). Within-method passes that do not survive this check: Empirical Quantile Mapping Mar, Gamma Quantile Mapping Feb, Gamma Quantile Mapping Mar, Power Transformation May, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Feb, Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling Mar and Variance Scaling (unbounded) Feb.

Empirical Quantile Mapping reproduces the CHIRPS distribution and, with the dry policy, its dry share (totals ≤ 1 mm: Feb 12.9% vs CHIRPS 12.9%); it passes the screening for Feb and Mar, but its FMAM amount skill is lower than Mean-Variance Scaling (-0.018 vs -0.007). A possible explanation is sampling noise in an empirical quantile function built from 23 CHIRPS values per fold; the results do not isolate it.

Scaled Distribution Mapping follows the published algorithm (Switanek et al. 2017, steps 1–7; checked numerically against an independent implementation of the steps). Where the model is drier than CHIRPS it cannot add rain: in Feb 58% of model members exceed 1 mm against 87% of CHIRPS years, and SDM, by design, keeps the model’s number of rain members, so its corrected dry share is 44% (CHIRPS 13%).

The methods that use the forecast’s own distribution (Detrended Quantile Mapping, Quantile Delta Mapping, Scaled Distribution Mapping, CDF-transform) score lower on FMAM terciles (-0.045 to -0.023 vs +0.005) and none passes the season screening. A possible explanation is that the distribution of a single forecast’s 25–51 members is a noisy estimate of the “future” distribution these methods were designed for; the results do not isolate the cause. Where model quantiles are dry, QDM falls back to the CHIRPS quantile (members affected: Feb 42% and Mar 18%), so its quantile changes are only partly preserved.

Published probabilities: confirmed better than Mean-Variance Scaling: Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling (Feb). Choosing the method each year from training-only scores, the probability procedure (SEL-P) scores FMAM blended RPSS +0.020 against +0.021, confirmed for Feb. Amounts: the amount procedure (SEL-A) scores CRPSS -0.011 against -0.007, confirmed for Feb and Mar; fixed methods confirmed against the family of all declared methods and targets: none.

The climatology blend narrows the differences. Across the methods, FMAM RPSS (1993–2016) spans 0.010 after the blend against 0.051 for the unblended screening counts. A better amount correction is trusted more by the blend: in Mar the fitted weight on climatology is 0.47 with Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling against 0.71 with Mean-Variance Scaling.

Choosing by training scores can backfire. For Apr, SEL-P chose Linear Scaling from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.000, 95% interval -0.004 to +0.004; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 4 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2021 and 2020); for May, SEL-P chose Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling from the 1993–2016 scores; over 2017–2025 it has a worse mean RPS (Δ +0.001, 95% interval -0.006 to +0.009; better than Mean-Variance Scaling in 5 of 9 years, with the largest losses in 2021 and 2025). These choices fail the no-harm rule; where the interval includes 0 they do not establish a significant deterioration. A method that ranks first on the training years is not, on that alone, a replacement.

No cell of All Ethiopia has exactly 0 mm in every training year, for any target, at 0.25° with CHIRPS. The all-zero guard (a separate MVS variant, outside the declared family) therefore never acts and equals Mean-Variance Scaling: the non-zero totals that Mean-Variance Scaling gives where every training year is 0 mm (its spread ratio cannot fall below 0.5) do not arise in these data. The guard remains a documented option; a finite history of zero rainfall does not make rain impossible.
observations: CHIRPS v3.0 monthly totals, averaged from 0.05° to 0.25°

config_contents.name: feb_fmam
config_contents.description: Rainfall-amount bias-correction benchmark: February-initialized ECMWF SEAS5, FMAM season and its calendar months, every 0.25 deg cell of Ethiopia (docs/47).

benchmark.gate_rule: Screening rule (docs/36 rule applied as a screen): a method passes for a target and score if, on the leave-one-year-out 1993-2016 per-year scores, its mean improvement over mvs has a one-sided sign-flip p-value below 0.05 after Holm adjustment, and its mean score over 2017-2025 (fits on 1993-2016) is not worse. 'screen_pass': Holm across the 5 targets of one method. 'screen_pass_family': Holm across every method and target of the benchmark for that score. A screening pass is not an operational adoption decision (see the confirmation run).

raw.label: Raw ECMWF (no correction)
raw.definition: x' = x (the uncorrected model; baseline, not a candidate)

ls.label: Linear Scaling
ls.definition: x' = x * mu_obs / mu_model (multiplicative mean correction; ratio 1 where mu_model < 0.1 mm)

mvs.label: Mean-Variance Scaling (operational)
mvs.definition: x' = max(0, mu_obs + r (x - mu_model)), r = clip(sd_obs/sd_model, 0.5, 2); r = 1 if sd_model < 1 mm

vs.label: Variance Scaling (unbounded)
vs.definition: Same algebra and the same r = 1 fallback (sd_model < 1 mm) as MVS, without the 0.5-2 ratio limits

sqrt_mvs.label: Square-root-space Mean-Variance Scaling
sqrt_mvs.definition: MVS applied to sqrt(x) (r limits 0.5-2; r = 1 if the sqrt-space sd < 0.1), clipped at 0 and squared back (docs/36)

pt.label: Power Transformation
pt.definition: x' = a x^b: b (0.1-3) matches the coefficient of variation where reachable (bound hits reported), a the mean

dc.label: Delta Change
dc.definition: Training-year CHIRPS totals times a = forecast ensemble mean / model mean (a in 0.2-5): historical scenarios, not corrected members

loci.label: Local Intensity Scaling
loci.definition: Model threshold with the observed frequency of totals above 1 mm, then intensity scaling above it (designed for daily rainfall; here monthly or seasonal totals)

eqm.label: Empirical Quantile Mapping
eqm.definition: x' = Q_obs(F_model(x)) with the dry policy; constant-ratio extrapolation outside the training range

gqm.label: Gamma Quantile Mapping
gqm.definition: x' = G_obs^-1(G_model(x)), G = dry mass (<= 1 mm) + gamma by weighted maximum likelihood, with the dry policy; linear scaling where fewer than 3 wet values

dqm.label: Detrended Quantile Mapping
dqm.definition: a * EQM(x / a), a = forecast ensemble mean / model mean (0.2-5): removes and reapplies the bounded ratio; exact preservation of the final mean anomaly is not guaranteed

qdm.label: Quantile Delta Mapping
qdm.definition: x' = Q_obs(tau) * x / Q_model(tau), tau = rank of x in the forecast ensemble; change capped at 5 and replaced by Q_obs(tau) where Q_model(tau) <= 1 mm (both reported), so preservation is partial there

sdm.label: Scaled Distribution Mapping
sdm.definition: Switanek et al. (2017) precipitation steps 1-7: gamma fits, recurrence intervals interpolated to the forecast's length, scaled CDF, rain-member count; model climatology with equal-year weights

cdft.label: CDF-transform
cdft.definition: F_obs,f = F_obs(F_model^-1(F_forecast)); x' = F_obs,f^-1(F_forecast(x)); implementation choices: model and forecast first scaled to the CHIRPS mean, values stay within the scaled forecast range

mvs_zero_guard.label: MVS with all-zero guard (variant)
mvs_zero_guard.definition: Operational MVS, but corrected totals are 0 mm where every training year has exactly 0 mm (a documented modelling choice, not a physical rule)

config_contents.name: feb_fmam_ratio_limits
config_contents.description: MVS ratio-limit study: February-initialized ECMWF SEAS5, FMAM season and its calendar months, every 0.25 deg cell of Ethiopia (docs/47). Operational MVS (spread ratio limited to 0.5-2) against the same correction with limits 1/3-3, 1/4-4 and none.

mvs.definition: x' = max(0, mu_obs + r (x - mu_model)), r = clip(sd_obs/sd_model, 0.5, 2); r = 1 if sd_model < 1 mm

mvs_r3.label: MVS, ratio limits 1/3-3
mvs_r3.definition: x' = max(0, mu_obs + r (x - mu_model)), r = clip(sd_obs/sd_model, 0.5, 2); r = 1 if sd_model < 1 mm; parameters {'ratio_bounds': [0.3333333333333333, 3.0], 'min_model_sd': 1.0}

mvs_r4.definition: x' = max(0, mu_obs + r (x - mu_model)), r = clip(sd_obs/sd_model, 0.5, 2); r = 1 if sd_model < 1 mm; parameters {'ratio_bounds': [0.25, 4.0], 'min_model_sd': 1.0}

vs.label: Variance Scaling (unbounded)

recommendation_rule.description: Rule by which the platform suggests a bias-correction method for each cycle, target and product (scripts/bias_recommend.py, docs/47). Fixed before the independent validation seasons are scored. A suggestion is advice for a decision; it never changes the published forecast.
recommendation_rule.historical: A method is a candidate only if the confirmation (CHIRPS, outer leave-one-year-out over the training years, full pipeline) finds it better than the operational method with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 across every declared method and target, and not worse over the test years. Variants outside the declared family are not candidates.
recommendation_rule.choice: Among candidates, the method the selection-aware procedure chooses from all training years (training-only information); if that method is not a candidate, the candidate with the best training-period score. Other candidates are listed as alternatives: a confirmation establishes improvement against the operational method, not a ranking among candidates.

validation.rule: Independent validation seasons are forecast years scored after the benchmark (bias_validation.py). A candidate is 'recommended' once at least minimum_seasons have been scored for it and the operational method, and its mean score over them is not worse; with fewer seasons it stays a 'candidate'; with enough seasons and a worse mean it is 'not supported by validation'.

statuses.keep: Keep the operational method: no method is confirmed better on the historical evidence.
statuses.candidate: Confirmed better on the historical evidence; independent validation seasons are still being collected.
statuses.recommended: Confirmed better on the historical evidence and not worse over the independent validation seasons.
statuses.not_supported: Confirmed better on the historical evidence but worse over the independent validation seasons.
